reconcile.title: Reconcile
reconcile.intro: Match purchase charges against the finance transactions that paid for them.
reconcile.keys.hint: j / k to move · enter to accept · x to reject
reconcile.truncated: Showing the first {{limit}} charges. More arrive as you work through these.
reconcile.empty.title: Nothing is waiting on you
reconcile.empty.hint: Every charge in this filter is already decided or auto-linked. Widen the filter to see the rest.
reconcile.error.title: Could not load the reconcile queue
reconcile.action.caveat: Accepting pins the link so no later sweep revises it. Rejecting only removes the link — nothing records the rejection yet, so the next sweep may propose it again.
reconcile.status.rejected: Link removed. The next sweep may propose it again.
reconcile.entry.noProposals: Nothing proposed — this charge is unexplained.

merchants.period.label: Period
merchants.currency.noTotal: The roll-up gave no total for this currency. The merchants below are still its own figures, so they are shown rather than dropped.
merchants.split.meterLabel: Share of spend explained by a matched charge
merchants.split.overLinked: More has been linked to these orders than they came to, so no share of the total is meaningful.
merchants.attribution.title: How these merchants are grouped
merchants.attribution.name: Grouped by name
merchants.attribution.explain.entity: Grouped on a contacts entity id, the operative identity. The label shown is the one from the group's newest order, ranked as text — a merchant renamed since then can still be wearing its older name (POPS-1854).
merchants.attribution.explain.name: Grouped on the merchant's label because no entity is attached, so this is a label total, not an entity total. Two merchants sharing a label share this row, and renaming one splits its history. No export adapter resolves a merchant entity today, so every exported order lands here (POPS-1852).
merchants.attribution.explain.unattribut: The order names no merchant. Kept as its own group rather than dropped, so the groups still add up to the spend.
merchants.drilldown.error.title: Could not load this merchant's orders
merchants.drilldown.none_one: The roll-up counted {{count}} order here, and the order index returned none. The two reads disagree — do not read either as complete.
merchants.drilldown.none_other: The roll-up counted {{count}} orders here, and the order index returned none. The two reads disagree — do not read either as complete.
merchants.drilldown.capped: Showing the first {{shown}} of the {{counted}} orders in this total. The list is at the page limit, so the rest are past it and the list above is not the whole of the figures above it.
merchants.drilldown.short: Showing {{shown}} orders, and the roll-up counted {{counted}}. The list is not at the page limit, so the two reads disagree — do not read either as complete.
merchants.drilldown.over: Showing {{shown}} orders, and the roll-up counted {{counted}}. The list holds more orders than the figures above were computed from — do not read either as complete.
merchants.absent.title: Not built below this layer

merchants.absent.items: Line items, per-item buy count and last bought need a product-grain aggregate (POPS-1849).
merchants.absent.inventory: Whether an item is already in inventory needs the inventory fan-out (POPS-245).

receipts.drop.multiPart: A long receipt can be photographed in several frames. Add up to {{max}} of them — they are one purchase, read in the order below.

products.title: Product dictionary
products.intro: What this pillar has learned about product identity: one product per thing you recognise, and every printed wording that resolves to it. A correction here applies to every line that ever printed that wording.
products.error.title: Could not load the product dictionary
products.empty.title: The dictionary is empty
products.empty.hint: Nothing has been learned yet, so every aggregate groups lines by their printed name exactly as it did before this existed. Run the proposal pass to write down the groupings that are already there.
products.filtered.title: Nothing matches this filter
products.filtered.hint: The dictionary holds entries, but none under this source with this assertion. Widen the filter to see the rest.
products.history.caveat: Nothing here is written to a line. A product's grouping is resolved fresh on every read, so a correction applies to the orders already stored as well as the ones still to arrive — order counts, cadence and unit-price history for these products are recomputed under the new grouping the next time anything reads them. The one thing a correction does not revisit is a line's item kind: that pass writes its decision onto the line, and a regrouping made afterwards does not re-open it.
products.assertion.explain.asserted: A person asserted every wording here. The proposal pass may not retire, repoint or relabel any of them.
products.assertion.explain.partAsserted: Some wordings here were asserted and some are still the pass's proposals, so this product is unfinished work — anything summarising it reports it as a proposal.
products.assertion.explain.proposed: The proposal pass minted every wording here and nobody has vouched for one. A later pass may retire any of them once no line prints that wording, and a product its last wording leaves is deleted with it. Naming a product holds its wordings back from exactly that, so a name you typed is never lost to a pass.
products.action.forgetWordingConfirm: Forget it, and the product with it
products.pass.title: The proposal pass
products.pass.explain: Reads every stored line, mints an entry for each printed wording that has none, and retires the unasserted entries no line prints any more. A wording somebody asserted is left alone, and so are the wordings reaching a product somebody named. Nothing runs this on a schedule — it runs when you press the button.
products.status.merge: Pointed at that product. Every line printing that wording groups there now, the ones already stored included.
products.status.split: Given a product of its own again.
products.status.assert: Asserted. The proposal pass may no longer touch that wording.
products.status.retract: Retracted. That wording is a proposal again, and a pass may retire it.
products.status.forgetWording: Wording forgotten. Its lines fall back to grouping on the printed name.
products.status.forgetWordingWithProduct: Wording forgotten, and the product it was the last one reaching — the name somebody typed for that product is gone with it. Its lines fall back to grouping on the printed name.
products.status.rename: Renamed. The wordings that resolve to it are untouched, and the product is now beyond the proposal pass's reach: a pass will not retire the wordings reaching it, so the name cannot be swept away with them.
products.status.forgetProduct: Product forgotten, and every wording with it.
products.action.forgetWordingConfirmName: Forget {{wording}}, and the product {{label}} with it
products.action.forgetProductConfirmName: Forget {{label}} and every wording that reaches it
